title: Fed hikes rates to 3.75%-4% in first increase since 2023
content:
The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to a target range of **3.75%-4%** on 16 September 2026, its first hike since 2023, with all 12 voting members backing the move. The decision followed hotter-than-expected CPI and PPI data and a bond sell-off that had pushed the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%. In its updated dot plot, 16 of 18 officials signalled at least one further hike by year-end, with the median projection at **4.00%-4.25%**.

Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation "remains too high" and that the Fed is "serious about delivering price stability," offering little near-term relief. Equities swung on the announcement before steadying, while Treasury yields stayed elevated as markets priced a more prolonged tightening cycle extending into 2027.

title: BoE holds rates at 3.75%, diverging from Fed and ECB hikes
content:
The Bank of England kept Bank Rate at **3.75%** on 17 September 2026, a sixth straight hold, as the MPC voted 6-3 against three members who wanted a 25bp rise. The decision put the BoE at odds with both the Fed, which had hiked a day earlier, and the ECB, which raised its deposit rate to 2.5% on 10 September. UK CPI rose to 3.1% in August, and the BoE paused all gilt sales until April 2027 while ending long-dated gilt sales permanently.

Sterling fell broadly after the announcement, with GBP/USD testing lows near **1.3360**, while the 30-year gilt yield dropped more than 10bp on the QT overhaul. The BoE signalled a "hawkish pause," leaving the door open to further tightening if energy-driven inflation persists into next year.

title: Wall Street logs second losing week as 10-year yield tops 5%
content:
US equities closed a volatile week to 18 September 2026 with the Dow down around **1.5%**, its worst week since March, while the S&P 500 slipped roughly 0.1% for a second straight weekly decline. The 10-year Treasury yield touched **5.04%** intraweek, its highest since 2007, as the Fed's rate hike and oil prices near a four-month high of **$106/bbl** compounded pressure on risk assets.

Rate-sensitive and AI-linked tech shares were among the hardest hit, though a Thursday rebound, the Nasdaq 100's best day in six weeks, limited losses. Strategists flagged the 5% threshold on the 10-year as one that has historically preceded a more durable equity headwind.
